issues.problem: Overstated 'first'. Slide says: "DeepMind says it is the **first** real-time world model to generate audio natively." DeepMind's blog says: "Genie 4 is our first real-time world model to generate audio natively." Dropping 'our' turns a first for DeepMind into a first for the whole industry. TechCrunch also reports that Runway's GWM Worlds 2, released a couple of months earlier, is "a playable model that responds dynamically to user inputs and includes audio generation", so neither source supports an industry first.
issues.fix: Replace the last sentence with: "DeepMind calls it **its first** real-time world model to generate audio natively." (body goes from 35 to 34 words)

issues.problem: A paraphrase is shown as a quote and credited to the wrong speaker. The title "\"Still early days\"" uses quotation marks, and the body adds "So says the team behind it." Neither article quotes anyone saying those words. TechCrunch reports them in indirect speech from one person: "Throughout the briefing, Rivas stressed that it’s still early days for Genie 4 and that it’s not yet clear what the end-to-end product experience will be." (Diego Rivas, "a Google DeepMind engineer"). DeepMind's blog says: "it remains an early, experimental model" and "Genie 4 remains an early, evolving area of research."
issues.fix: Title: Still early days (no quotation marks). Replace "So says the team behind it." with "DeepMind calls Genie 4 an early, experimental model." (body becomes 44 words). To keep TechCrunch's version instead, write without quotation marks: "Google DeepMind engineer Diego Rivas stressed it is still early days, TechCrunch reports." That adds words, so trim elsewhere to stay within 45.

issues.problem: Same misquote and wrong speaker: "The team says it is 'still early days'". TechCrunch: "Rivas stressed that it’s still early days for Genie 4" (indirect speech, not a quote). Also, "haven't worked out" drops TechCrunch's hedge: "they still haven’t quite figured out how to ensure the audio will be accurate and any in-world text will be legible."
issues.fix: "Diego Rivas, a Google DeepMind engineer, stressed during the briefing that it's still early days for Genie 4 (TechCrunch's paraphrase, not a direct quote). The team also acknowledged gaps: details and objects can drift the longer a simulation runs, and they still haven't quite figured out how to ensure the audio will be accurate and any in-world text will be legible."
